vulnerability_patterns.description: Possible duplicate deallocation on the AES-processing error path if `buffer` is also released by another cleanup path or owner.
trigger_conditions: `from_buffer` is false so the removed `_zip_buffer_free(buffer)` would execute
another path still frees or assumes ownership of `buffer` after this return
fix_patterns: Remove branch-local deallocation from error path
Preserve single authoritative owner for `buffer` lifetime
Avoid duplicate cleanup when ownership is external or handled later
evidence_lines: In `lib/zip_dirent.c`, the patch deletes `if (!from_buffer) { _zip_buffer_free(buffer); }` immediately before `return -1;` on `_zip_dirent_process_winzip_aes` failure.

vulnerability_patterns.description: Possible stale use if `buffer` was freed in this local branch but later referenced by caller-side or enclosing cleanup/state handling after the function returns `-1`.
trigger_conditions: `buffer` remains reachable by surrounding state or caller after this function returns
fix_patterns: Explicitly avoid early invalidation on local error path
Keep resource alive until authoritative owner performs cleanup
Prefer single-point teardown over branch-specific freeing
evidence_lines: The only semantic change is deletion of `_zip_buffer_free(buffer)` from the AES-processing failure branch in `lib/zip_dirent.c`, indicating that freeing here was considered unsafe.

suggestions: Model `buffer` ownership precisely across success and failure paths instead of classifying from the presence of `_zip_buffer_free` alone.
Prefer detecting inconsistent branch-local cleanup versus authoritative owner cleanup on return paths.
Check whether `buffer` is later freed by common epilogue or caller; if yes, prioritize duplicate-free findings.
Check whether any state still retains `buffer` after this branch; if yes, prioritize premature-free/use-after-free findings.
Avoid using null/non-null or `from_buffer` alone as proof of safe lifetime; require ownership evidence.
Prefer fix-shape reasoning: removed local deallocation on error path suggests centralizing teardown at a single authoritative lifecycle point.

analysis_rationale: The patch in `lib/zip_dirent.c` only removes a conditional call to `_zip_buffer_free(buffer)` on the `_zip_dirent_process_winzip_aes(zde, error)` failure path. This is concrete evidence of a lifecycle correction on an error path, but the excerpt alone does not prove whether the removed free previously caused a double free, a use-after-free, or another ownership/lifetime bug elsewhere. The strongest evidence-backed conclusion is that the fix avoids freeing `buffer` in this branch because ownership or later cleanup is handled elsewhere.
